sentences.show: A metal ball, 58 centimetres wide, beeped from space. And America was afraid.
It launched on this day in 1957: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite.
It circled the Earth every 96 minutes.
Anyone with a shortwave radio could hear it.
But the rocket that carried it could also carry a nuclear warhead, anywhere in the world, in minutes.
America's answer was the Vanguard rocket.
It failed. Then it failed again.
The fear created NASA, and poured money into science and schools.
Two American physicists listened to Sputnik's beeps, and realised they could tell exactly where it was.
That idea grew into satellite navigation.
Sputnik's batteries died after three weeks.
It fell back to Earth on 4 January, after 1,440 orbits.
